body.heading: Your body, word by word
paragraphs: You carry this chart around with you everywhere — it IS you. Body words help you tell a doctor where it hurts, follow a dance move, and understand how you work.
Touch each part as you read about it.

body.heading: Head and face
paragraphs: Your head holds your brain, your thinking machine. On your face: eyes for seeing, ears for hearing, a nose for smelling, a mouth for tasting, talking and smiling.
Your chin is the bottom of your face, and your cheeks are the soft parts on either side of your smile.

body.heading: Arms and hands
paragraphs: Shoulders connect your arms to your body. Your elbow is the bendy joint in the middle of your arm. Your wrist connects your hand to your arm.
Each hand has five fingers — and one special finger called the thumb, which helps you grip, hold and give a thumbs-up.

body.heading: Legs and feet
paragraphs: Your hips connect your legs to your body. Your knee is the bendy joint in the middle of your leg. Your ankle connects your foot to your leg.
Feet carry you everywhere. Your heel is at the back, your toes are at the front — ten toes in all, wiggling in your shoes.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Play body-words Simon Says with the tricky ones: 'Touch your elbow! Touch your wrist! Touch your chin!'
2. Which body part do you think works the hardest every day — your heart, your legs or your brain? Defend your answer!

takeaway: Body words — chin, cheeks, elbow, wrist, knee, ankle, heel — let you describe exactly where things are and how you move.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
